# Building B — seismic diaphragm shears and shear wall loads

You are the delegated design engineer for the lateral load path of **Building B** at the
Continental Divide Data Center in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. The shell is erected: the
precast wall panels are up, the roof deck is laid, and the Engineer of Record has issued the
project documents to you in `project/`, with the published standards available on this project in
`library/`.

Building B is a one-storey box. The exterior walls are 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete
panels that span vertically from the foundation to the roof and cantilever above it to the top of
the parapet; they are the only seismic force-resisting elements. The roof is a bare steel deck
diaphragm on open-web joists, pierced by a mechanical well and a skylight band, and it carries six
roof-top units.

**The Engineer of Record has not selected the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the
chords and collectors, the panel connections or the anchorage. That is your scope.** Design it,
analyse it, and hand over the package below.

## What you are asked to produce

Write these five files, then zip them (no enclosing folder) to `output/submission.zip`:

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `design_record.json` | the machine-readable design and the quantities you report |
| `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | the plan drawings for the delegated design engineer |
| `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | the calculation package |
| `constraint_register.xlsx` | the requirements you applied, with their sources |
| `design_basis.md` | the design basis narrative |

Templates for all five, with the exact keys, sheet names and layer names, are in `templates/`.
Start from them. **Write a first complete version of all five files early — within roughly your
first 100 steps — and improve it afterwards; a package that is never written scores zero.**

### `diaphragm_plan.dxf`

Two plan views of the roof, one for **E-W** loading and one for **N-S** loading, in feet, showing
for each direction:

* the **seismic roof diaphragm shear** — the distributed diaphragm force `w_px` in **plf** along
  the building, and the design unit shear in each deck attachment zone;
* the **applied shear wall load `F_x` in kips** on each of the four exterior wall lines;
* the chord, collector and drag strut runs with their design axial forces;
* the deck attachment zone boundaries with the pattern assigned to each zone;
* a revision block, and a statement of whether the package is ASD or LRFD.

Required layers: `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR`, `WALL_FORCE`, `CHORD`, `COLLECTOR`, `DECK_ZONE`, `GRID`,
`TITLE`.

### `seismic_calculations.xlsx`

Sheets `WEIGHTS`, `BASE_SHEAR`, `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES`, `WALL_FORCES`, `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE`,
`CHORD_FORCES`, covering the effective seismic weight, the seismic response coefficient, the
vertical distribution, the diaphragm design forces, the transfer of the inertia of the wall
cantilevering above the deck, the chord forces, and the force on every wall line for every design
case the criteria list.

### `constraint_register.xlsx`

One row per requirement you applied: the **document**, the **clause, table or section**, the
**value**, and the **items it binds**. It is scored on how many of the governing requirements you
found and cited, and on whether you cited them correctly — rows whose source is a superseded
document, another building or another load case count against you, while extra correct rows do
not. A register that reaches fewer than **60 %** of the governing requirements loses that credit
entirely. A hard requirement you never registered is treated as one you never applied.

### `design_basis.md`

State, with the clause you relied on: the seismic force-resisting system you selected and why it
is the cost-efficient choice; how you resolved every conflict you found between the documents;
the governing check on each wall line; the alternatives you rejected; and the installed cost of
your scope against the budget.

## How your design is judged

Your design is re-analysed by the project's own protocol and checked against every requirement in
the project documents, on design cases you are not shown as well as the ones you are. Within the
requirements, the cheaper installed cost of the lateral scope wins: the score rewards a design
that satisfies everything at the lowest cost, and a design that violates a safety or capacity
requirement keeps none of its cost credit. Each design case scores 0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O, where p
is the fraction of the 34 constraint families that count, h the fraction of the 21 hard families
that count (a family counts when the design satisfies it and every hard requirement that governs it
is in your register; [h = 1] is 1 when all 21 count, else 0), and O is a certified lower bound on
the installed cost divided by your installed cost, at most 1. The score is the mean over the design
cases.

Units are feet, kips and plf unless a document says otherwise. Where the documents disagree, find
the reading the project record supports and say which you took.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

Continental Divide Digital Infrastructure LLC - Owner's Basis of Design (extract)
Project: Continental Divide Data Center - Building B   Document OBD-CDDC-B Rev 4   2026-08-14
1.4 Tenancy and occupancy
Building B houses the primary data hall and, on its east side, the Lewis and Clark County consolidated 911 emergency communications tenant, including the dispatch floor and the radio equipment room. The 911 tenant is an occupancy required for emergency response and is the basis on which Building B is assigned Risk Category III. Building A, which has no emergency tenant, remains Risk Category II.
2.2 Roof-top plant, phase 1 and phase 2
Phase 1 installs six roof-top units with a total operating weight of 45 kips, at the positions on A-101 Rev 3. Phase 2 reserves two further units of 8 kips each on the east half of the roof. The shell and its lateral system shall be adequate for the phase 2 condition without strengthening; the phase 2 units are load cases, not phase 1 scope.
3.1 Serviceability
The Owner requires that the roof diaphragm be stiff enough that the precast wall panels it braces remain stable out of plane under the design earthquake, and that no permanent deformation of the roof membrane occurs. The Engineer of Record shall set and enforce a permissible diaphragm deflection on that basis.
5.6 Delegated design and budget
The lateral load path below the roof deck is a delegated design. The delegated designer selects the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the chords, collectors and drag struts, the panel connections and the anchorage. The scope carries a hard capital cap; see PROC-114. Designs that exceed the cap will not be accepted.
=== DOCX: project/00_admin/RFI-041_Dock_Opening_As_Built.docx ===
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 041
Project: Continental Divide Data Center - Building B    RFI-041    Opened 2026-08-10    Status: CLOSED
Question (Erector)
Dock opening D-3 on the south wall was set out from the east face of panel S-09 rather than from grid 3 as detailed on PC-101 Rev 2. The erected clear opening at D-3 measures 15 ft 6 in against the 14 ft 0 in detailed, and panel S-12 and everything east of it in that band sits 1 ft 6 in east of the detailed joint line, which closes the pier between D-4 and D-5 to 14 ft 6 in. The erected positions are recorded in ERL-2026-08 and are in the 7 August scan. Confirm whether the panels are to be reset.
Response (Engineer of Record)
The panels are not to be reset. The erected geometry is accepted as the as-built condition. The delegated lateral design shall be based on the erected geometry recorded in the scan and the erection log, not on the detailed dimensions of PC-101. Note that this changes the length of the full-height piers on the south wall and therefore the distribution of shear to the wall lines. The same applies to louver L-2 on the north wall, which was cast to shop ticket Rev B at 16 ft, and to the west electrical yard opening EY-1, which was widened on site to 44 ft for the generator bus duct.
Architectural sheet A-101 Rev 3 note 6 already directs the reader to the as-built survey for erected dimensions.

dense silty sand and gravel over weathered argillite.

The time-averaged shear wave velocity in the upper 100 ft is Vs,100 = 905 ft/s. Under the site class table of ASCE/SEI
7-22 Chapter 20 this parcel is Site Class D. Site-specific ground motion analysis is not triggered for this site class at
this S1.
This report supersedes, for the Building B parcel, any earlier site classification prepared for the adjacent Parcel 4B.

9. FOUNDATIONS

designed for 4,500 psf allowable bearing. Tie-down resistance for the precast panel base connections may use the
footing dead weight plus 0.45 times the vertical effective stress on the footing keyway.

TITLE         AS-BUILT SURVEY AND SCAN CONTROL REPORT                           ISSUED BY   Helena Valley Survey Associates




2. SCAN
The interior of the Building B shell was scanned on 7 August 2026 from eleven set-ups and registered into a single
point cloud. The delivered cloud is in the scanner's own coordinate frame, not the building grid. Units are feet.
The intensity channel is scaled 0 to 255.

3. CONTROL
Four 6 in high-reflectance spherical targets were set on the slab and coordinated from the building control line. They
return an intensity above 240 and are the only objects in the cloud that do. Their coordinates in the BUILDING GRID
are:
TARGET               X (ft)                  Y (ft)                    Z (ft)

CP-1                 6.50                    4.25                      5.40

                           Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT         DAP-2                                      REVISION   1   DATE        2026-07-31

TITLE            DIAPHRAGM ANALYSIS PROTOCOL                               ISSUED BY   Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC




1. PURPOSE
This protocol defines the analysis every delegated lateral design for Building B is checked against. It fixes the model,
the member properties, the load application and the reduction of the computed field to design values, so that two
engineers analysing the same design obtain the same design quantities. Designs are verified against this protocol; a
design whose own analysis differs from it will be assessed on the protocol's results.

2. THE TWO STAGES
Stage A is the in-plane model of a wall segment - a continuous run of precast panels between openings. Stage B is
the in-plane model of the roof diaphragm, supported on springs whose stiffnesses come from Stage A.

3. STAGE A - JOINTED PRECAST WALL SEGMENT
Each panel in a segment is a cantilever fixed at the foundation and free at the top, with three degrees of freedom at its
top: lateral displacement u, vertical displacement v and rotation θ. The cantilever height is the height to the roof
diaphragm (the parapet above the diaphragm is not part of the in-plane cantilever). Flexural and shear flexibility are
both included:
  fuu = h³/(3EI) + h/(GAv), fuθ = h²/(2EI), fθθ = h/EI,   kvv = EA/h

with Ec = 57,000√f'c psi for f'c = 6000 psi, Gc = Ec/2.4, Av = 5/6 of the gross area, and I taken as 0.50 Ig (cracked, ACI
318-19 Table 6.6.3.1.1(a)). The axial stiffness uses the gross area. A segment interrupted over part of its height by an
opening that does not reach the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are
factored by the solid fraction of the height.

Adjacent panels are connected by the vertical shear spring formed by their joint connectors: the spring stiffness is the
number of connectors in the joint times the connector stiffness of the manufacturer's table, and it acts on the relative
vertical slip of the two panel edges,
  slip = (vi + θi Li/2) − (vi+1 − θi+1 Li+1/2).

The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement. Condensing the
segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness kseg; recovering the internal state for a unit segment
force gives the shear in every joint and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force. A panel's tie-down
carries its own base couple, taken on an internal lever arm of 0.8 times the panel length, plus the coupling axial force
delivered to it.

4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
  D = diag(A′, A′, G′)

where G′ is the diaphragm shear stiffness of the attachment pattern assigned to the zone the element lies in, from the
manufacturer's diaphragm table, and A′ = 1740 kip/in is the smeared in-plane axial rigidity of the bare deck sheet
(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.
 Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.

5. LOADS
The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor Ax is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall
lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.

6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES
6.1 Zone design shear. The design unit shear of an attachment zone is the largest SECTION mean in that zone: for
every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.
6.2 Deflections and drift are taken from the semi-rigid model, with the real stiffness of the design. Forces are taken
from the envelope of Section 6.3.
6.3 Envelope. Every design force - zone shear, wall line force, wall segment force, chord and collector axial force - is
the largest of the three idealisations:
  flexible: the diaphragm is a simple beam spanning between the two wall lines that resist the direction of loading; the unit shear at a
section is the beam shear divided by the net diaphragm depth at that section, and the chord force is the beam moment divided by the
same depth. Accidental torsion is not transferred in the flexible idealisation.

  rigid: the Stage B model with the membrane rigidities multiplied by 107.

  semi-rigid: the Stage B model as built.

6.4 Orthogonal cases. For the cases the design criteria mark 100/30, the demands are those of the case direction
plus 0.30 times the demands of the companion case in the orthogonal direction with the same mass case, same sign
of accidental eccentricity and same stage.
 APPENDIX A - VERIFICATION EXAMPLE VP-1
An implementation of this protocol that reproduces the following Stage A result is consistent with the reference
implementation. No other verification values are published.

Case. A single wall segment 40.0 ft long, on a wall line with no openings within the segment, built from four 10.0 ft
panels, 8 in solid normal-weight precast, cantilever height 28.0 ft to the diaphragm, f'c = 6,000 psi, cracked flexural
rigidity per Section 3, joints connected by three RPC-40 connectors each (joint spring 3 x 320 = 960 kip/in).
QUANTITY                                                                             VALUE

segment lateral stiffness k_seg                                                      1,279.4 kip/in

shear in joint 1 (end joint), per kip of segment force                               0.2630 kip/kip

shear in joint 2 (middle joint), per kip of segment force                            0.2527 kip/kip

base moment of panel 1, per kip of segment force                                     88.91 kip-in/kip

                      Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT      PR-07                                  REVISION     -       DATE          2026-08-03

TITLE         STRUCTURAL PEER REVIEW - COMMENT AND RESOLUTION             ISSUED BY     Gallatin Peer Review Group LLC



To: Engineer of Record. Subject: Building B lateral system, review comment 7.

COMMENT 7

The roof diaphragm of Building B may be idealised as flexible under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1 because the
vertical elements are concrete shear walls and the deck is untopped steel. The reviewer does not accept a flexible
idealisation as the sole basis of design for this building. The roof is pierced by a 60 ft x 40 ft mechanical well and an
80 ft x 20 ft skylight band, the wall lines are very unequally pierced by openings - the west wall has a single 40 ft
electrical yard opening and the south wall has five dock doors - and the erected panel positions differ from the record
set. The centre of rigidity is therefore not at the centre of the plan and a tributary-width distribution does not bound the
wall line forces.

REQUIREMENT

The design forces for the diaphragm, the collectors and the wall lines shall be the envelope of the flexible, rigid and
semi-rigid distributions, each computed by the project protocol DAP-2. The semi-rigid model shall use the erected
geometry, not the record geometry. Deflections shall be reported from the semi-rigid model.

RESOLUTION

Accepted by the Engineer of Record and incorporated in SDC-02 Rev 2 Section 10 and in protocol DAP-2. Closed.

                      Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT     SDC-02                                REVISION     2      DATE          2026-08-14

TITLE        STRUCTURAL DESIGN CRITERIA                                ISSUED BY     Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC




1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.

2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore Ie = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.

3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.

Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both SDS and SD1; the more severe governs.

4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, Ω0 and Cd and the
clause that permits it.

Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.

5. DIAPHRAGM DESIGN
 The roof diaphragm is a bare steel deck diaphragm and is designed by the traditional provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3 are not used on this project, and Section
12.10.4 is not used because the Owner's serviceability criterion in Section 7 below governs the diaphragm stiffness.
Note that the Section 12.10 Exception that bars Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 applies to precast concrete
diaphragms; the Building B roof diaphragm is steel deck, not precast.

Collectors, drag struts and their connections to the vertical elements are designed for the amplified force required for
this seismic design category. Continuous chords are required on all four diaphragm edges and on all four sides of
every roof opening. A continuous drag strut is required across every wall opening 12 ft wide or wider so that
diaphragm shear is delivered to the full-height piers.

6. STRUCTURAL WALLS AND THEIR ANCHORAGE
Anchorage of the precast wall panels to the roof diaphragm is designed to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1,
including the amplification ka for flexible diaphragms. The span of the flexible diaphragm Lf is determined as shown in
UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 (library). Continuous ties are required across the diaphragm; subdiaphragms used to
transfer the anchorage force to the continuous ties shall not exceed the length-to-depth ratio of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 12.11.2.2.1.

The panels span vertically from the foundation to the roof diaphragm and cantilever above it to the top of the parapet.
The weight tributary to the roof, and the anchorage force, shall account for the lever action of that cantilever; see the
worked one-storey bare-deck example in FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1 for the form of the tributary
calculation.

7. DRIFT AND DEFLECTION CRITERIA
Storey drift is limited to the allowable storey drift of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for this risk category ('all other
structures'), applied to the design storey drift of Section 12.8.6.
Diaphragm deflection. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.12.2 the deflection in the plane of the diaphragm shall not
exceed the permissible deflection of the attached elements. For Building B the attached elements are the precast wall
panels, whose out-of-plane stability governs. The Engineer of Record's permissible value is 4.0 in (approximately
h/84 for the 28 ft panel, from the out-of-plane slender-wall stability check of the panel under the design earthquake
displacement), applied to the design (amplified) deflection Cdδ/Ie of the top of the panel, that is the diaphragm
deflection plus the drift of the wall line supporting it.
 8. LOAD CASES TO BE REPORTED
Accidental torsion is applied as required by ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.8.4.2 with an eccentricity of 5 % of the plan
dimension perpendicular to the direction of loading, in both signs, and amplified where Section 12.8.4.3 requires it. In
addition to the two orthogonal directions, the Owner requires the 100 % / 30 % orthogonal combination to be reported
for the cases listed below. The construction-stage cases are the erector's temporary condition and use the reduced
construction-period seismic load of ERC-07.
CASE      DIRECTION     ACCIDENTAL ECCENTRICITY      MASS CASE      ORTHOGONAL       STAGE

S01       X             +1                           base           -                final

S02       X             -1                           base           -                final

S03       Y             +1                           base           -                final

S04       Y             -1                           base           -                final

S05       X             +1                           base           100/30           final

S06       Y             -1                           base           100/30           final

S07       X             +1                           future         -                final

S08       Y             +1                           future         -                final

S09       X             -1                           future         100/30           final

S10       Y             -1                           future         100/30           final

S11       X             +1                           erection       -                erection

S12       Y             -1                           erection       -                erection

The 'future' mass case includes the two phase-2 roof-top units reserved in the Owner's Basis of Design. The
delegated design shall be adequate for every case.

9. DESIGN FORMAT
The delegated designer may work in LRFD or in ASD. Every load and every capacity presented in the deliverable
shall be clearly identified as ASD or as LRFD, and the format shall be used consistently throughout the
package. Where an ASD package is presented, seismic load effects are 0.7E and capacities are the allowable values
of the referenced material standard.

10. ANALYSIS
The structural peer reviewer requires the diaphragm force distribution to be the envelope of flexible, rigid and
semi-rigid behaviour; see PR-07. The analysis shall follow the project protocol DAP-2, which defines the model, the
properties, the application of the accidental torsion and the reduction of the computed field to design values. A
verification example is published in DAP-2 Appendix A.

11. DELEGATED DESIGN SCOPE AND BUDGET
The lateral scope covered by this delegated design is the deck attachment, the chords, collectors and drag struts, the
panel joint connectors, the panel base tie-downs, the wall-to-diaphragm anchorage and the seismic force-resisting
system detailing premium. Unit rates and the capital cap for that scope are in PROC-114. The installed cost of the
lateral scope shall not exceed the cap.

exit_code=0 === LIBRARY: library/29_CFR_1926.704_Precast_Concrete_eCFR.xml § 1926.704 Requirements for precast concrete.

(a) Precast concrete wall units, structural framing, and tilt-up wall panels shall be adequately supported to prevent overturning and to prevent collapse until permanent connections are completed.

(b) Lifting inserts which are embedded or otherwise attached to tilt-up precast concrete members shall be capable of supporting at least two times the maximum intended load applied or transmitted to them.

(c) Lifting inserts which are embedded or otherwise attached to precast concrete members, other than the tilt-up members, shall be capable of supporting at least four times the maximum intended load applied or transmitted to them.

(d) Lifting hardware shall be capable of supporting at least five times the maximum intended load applied or transmitted to the lifting hardware.

=== project/30_seismic/DAP-2_Diaphragm_Analysis_Protocol_REV1.pdf 3
  p0 (151.8,62.5): Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
  p0 (70.2,90.0): DOCUMENT
DAP-2
REVISION
1
DATE
2026-07-31
  p0 (70.2,106.0): TITLE
DIAPHRAGM ANALYSIS PROTOCOL
ISSUED BY
Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC
  p0 (67.2,140.7): 1. PURPOSE
  p0 (67.2,169.9): This protocol defines the analysis every delegated lateral design for Building B is checked against. It fixes the model,
the member properties, the load application and the reduction of the computed field to design values, so that two
engineers analysing the same design obtain the same design quantities. Designs are verified against this protocol; a
design whose own analysis differs from it will be assessed on the protocol's results.
  p0 (67.2,230.3): 2. THE TWO STAGES
  p0 (67.2,259.5): Stage A is the in-plane model of a wall segment - a continuous run of precast panels between openings. Stage B is
the in-plane model of the roof diaphragm, supported on springs whose stiffnesses come from Stage A.
  p0 (67.2,295.1): 3. STAGE A - JOINTED PRECAST WALL SEGMENT
  p0 (67.2,324.3): Each panel in a segment is a cantilever fixed at the foundation and free at the top, with three degrees of freedom at its
top: lateral displacement u, vertical displacement v and rotation θ. The cantilever height is the height to the roof
diaphragm (the parapet above the diaphragm is not part of the in-plane cantilever). Flexural and shear flexibility are
both included:
  p0 (67.2,380.0): fuu = h³/(3EI) + h/(GAv),   fuθ = h²/(2EI),   fθθ = h/EI,    kvv = EA/h
  p0 (67.2,396.1): with Ec = 57,000√f'c psi for f'c = 6000 psi, Gc = Ec/2.4, Av = 5/6 of the gross area, and I taken as 0.50 Ig (cracked, ACI
318-19 Table 6.6.3.1.1(a)). The axial stiffness uses the gross area. A segment interrupted over part of its height by an
opening that does not reach the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are
factored by the solid fraction of the height.
  p0 (67.2,451.7): Adjacent panels are connected by the vertical shear spring formed by their joint connectors: the spring stiffness is the
number of connectors in the joint times the connector stiffness of the manufacturer's table, and it acts on the relative
vertical slip of the two panel edges,
  p0 (67.2,495.0): slip = (vi + θi Li/2) − (vi+1 − θi+1 Li+1/2).
  p0 (67.2,511.1): The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement. Condensing the
segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness kseg; recovering the internal state for a unit segment
force gives the shear in every joint and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force. A panel's tie-down
carries its own base couple, taken on an internal lever arm of 0.8 times the panel length, plus the coupling axial force
delivered to it.
  p0 (67.2,583.9): 4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
  p0 (67.2,613.1): The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
  p0 (67.2,644.0): D = diag(A′, A′, G′)
  p0 (67.2,660.1): where G′ is the diaphragm shear stiffness of the attachment pattern assigned to the zone the element lies in, from the
manufacturer's diaphragm table, and A′ = 1740 kip/in is the smeared in-plane axial rigidity of the bare deck sheet
(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.
  p1 (67.2,62.9): Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.
  p1 (67.2,135.7): 5. LOADS
  p1 (67.2,164.9): The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
  p1 (67.2,220.5): Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor Ax is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall
lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.
  p1 (67.2,280.9): 6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES
  p1 (67.2,310.1): 6.1 Zone design shear. The design unit shear of an attachment zone is the largest SECTION mean in that zone: for
every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.
  p1 (67.2,365.7): 6.2 Deflections and drift are taken from the semi-rigid model, with the real stiffness of the design. Forces are taken
from the envelope of Section 6.3.
  p1 (67.2,396.5): 6.3 Envelope. Every design force - zone shear, wall line force, wall segment force, chord and collector axial force - is
the largest of the three idealisations:
  p1 (67.2,427.4): flexible: the diaphragm is a simple beam spanning between the two wall lines that resist the direction of loading; the unit shear at a
section is the beam shear divided by the net diaphragm depth at that section, and the chord force is the beam moment divided by the
same depth. Accidental torsion is not transferred in the flexible idealisation.
  p1 (67.2,461.7): rigid: the Stage B model with the membrane rigidities multiplied by 107.
  p1 (67.2,480.2): semi-rigid: the Stage B model as built.
  p1 (67.2,496.3): 6.4 Orthogonal cases. For the cases the design criteria mark 100/30, the demands are those of the case direction
plus 0.30 times the demands of the companion case in the orthogonal direction with the same mass case, same sign
of accidental eccentricity and same stage.
  p2 (67.2,62.7): APPENDIX A - VERIFICATION EXAMPLE VP-1
  p2 (67.2,91.9): An implementation of this protocol that reproduces the following Stage A result is consistent with the reference
implementation. No other verification values are published.
  p2 (67.2,122.7): Case. A single wall segment 40.0 ft long, on a wall line with no openings within the segment, built from four 10.0 ft
panels, 8 in solid normal-weight precast, cantilever height 28.0 ft to the diaphragm, f'c = 6,000 psi, cracked flexural
rigidity per Section 3, joints connected by three RPC-40 connectors each (joint spring 3 x 320 = 960 kip/in).
  p2 (70.2,167.0): QUANTITY
VALUE

=== project/30_seismic/PR-07_Peer_Review_Comment_7.pdf 1
  p0 (151.8,62.5): Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
  p0 (70.2,90.0): DOCUMENT
PR-07
REVISION
-
DATE
2026-08-03
  p0 (70.2,106.0): TITLE
STRUCTURAL PEER REVIEW - COMMENT AND RESOLUTION
ISSUED BY
Gallatin Peer Review Group LLC
  p0 (67.2,135.9): To: Engineer of Record. Subject: Building B lateral system, review comment 7.
  p0 (67.2,157.2): COMMENT 7
  p0 (67.2,181.3): The roof diaphragm of Building B may be idealised as flexible under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1 because the
vertical elements are concrete shear walls and the deck is untopped steel. The reviewer does not accept a flexible
idealisation as the sole basis of design for this building. The roof is pierced by a 60 ft x 40 ft mechanical well and an
80 ft x 20 ft skylight band, the wall lines are very unequally pierced by openings - the west wall has a single 40 ft
electrical yard opening and the south wall has five dock doors - and the erected panel positions differ from the record
set. The centre of rigidity is therefore not at the centre of the plan and a tributary-width distribution does not bound the
wall line forces.
  p0 (67.2,277.0): REQUIREMENT
  p0 (67.2,301.1): The design forces for the diaphragm, the collectors and the wall lines shall be the envelope of the flexible, rigid and
semi-rigid distributions, each computed by the project protocol DAP-2. The semi-rigid model shall use the erected
geometry, not the record geometry. Deflections shall be reported from the semi-rigid model.
  p0 (67.2,347.2): RESOLUTION
  p0 (67.2,371.3): Accepted by the Engineer of Record and incorporated in SDC-02 Rev 2 Section 10 and in protocol DAP-2. Closed.

  p0 (70.2,106.0): TITLE
STRUCTURAL DESIGN CRITERIA
ISSUED BY
Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC
  p0 (67.2,140.7): 1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
  p0 (67.2,169.9): The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
  p0 (67.2,225.5): A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.
  p0 (67.2,298.3): 2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
  p0 (67.2,327.5): Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore Ie = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.
  p0 (67.2,400.3): 3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
  p0 (67.2,429.5): The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.
  p0 (67.2,472.7): Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both SDS and SD1; the more severe governs.
  p0 (67.2,520.7): 4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
  p0 (67.2,549.9): The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, Ω0 and Cd and the
clause that permits it.
  p0 (67.2,630.3): Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.

7.1 Overview  
The 2020 Edition of the NEHRP Recommended Seismic Provisions for New Buildings and Other 
Structures (FEMA, 2020), referred to herein as the Provisions, includes three significant items 
related to the design of diaphragms that represent changes between the 2015 Provisions (FEMA, 
2016), and 2020 Provisions. These have resulted in matching changes between ASCE/SEI 7-16 
(ASCE, 2017) and ASCE/SEI 7-22 (ASCE, 2021). First, ASCE/SEI 7-16 Section 12.10.3 (Alternative 
Design Provisions for Diaphragms including Chords and Collectors) was expanded to permit use of 
bare steel deck diaphragms. Second, new Section 12.10.4 has been added, containing alternative 
diaphragm seismic design provisions for one-story structures with flexible diaphragms and rigid 
vertical elements (commonly designated as rigid-wall flexible-diaphragm (RWFD) buildings). Third, the 
ASCE/SEI 7-16 Section 12.10.3 alternative design provisions have been further expanded to permit 
use of concrete filled steel deck diaphragms. This is based in part on Resource Paper 6 in Part 3 of 
the 2020 NEHRP Provisions (FEMA P-1082-2).  
This chapter addresses use of the ASCE/SEI 7-22 diaphragm design provisions, including these 
three significant changes. The primary focus of this chapter is the determination of diaphragm 
seismic design forces. The horizontal distribution of these forces and design for shear and flexure 
are not addressed as this can vary depending on the classification of the diaphragm (flexible, semi-
rigid or rigid), the approach taken to analytical modeling of the structure, and the diaphragm system. 
In accordance with Section 12.3.4.1, rho () is assumed to be 1.0 for diaphragm design and 
therefore not included in this discussion. Similarly, effects that might be triggered by plan 
irregularities are not discussed. While these effects are ignored for the purposes of these example 
problems, such effects are required to be appropriately considered in design of structures. Further 
information on seismic design of diaphragms can be found in the NEHRP Seismic Design Technical 
Brief Series, as included in the other resources section that follows; while these briefs do not 
address the ASCE/SEI 7-22 revisions, they provide a wealth of information on other aspects of 
diaphragm design. 
 
1 Kelly Cobeen, S.E., Wiss, Janney, Elstner Associates, Inc.

Other Changes Between ASCE/SEI 7-16 and 7-22 
A number of other changes between ASCE/SEI 7-16 and 7-22 could potentially affect the 
design of diaphragms. Two in particular are worth mentioning in conjunction with diaphragm 
design: 
▪ 
First, significant changes have occurred to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.4, Seismic Ground 
Motion Values, including the inclusion of a multi-period response spectrum in Section 
11.4.5. For purposes of diaphragm design, it is intended, however, that the design spectral 
acceleration parameters of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.4.4 be used where SDS and SD1 
values are needed; for this reason, the change to Section 11.4.5 is not intended to affect 
diaphragm design.  
▪ 
Second, significant changes have been made to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Sections 12.8.6 and 
12.12, addressing deflection and drift. These changes do potentially affect diaphragm 
design and are discussed in this chapter. 
For further discussion of diaphragm deflections, the reader is referred to Section 7.2, FEMA P-
1026 (FEMA, 2021), Resource Paper 8 from FEMA P-2082-2, and the previously mentioned 
NEHRP Tech Brief series. 
The following are included in this chapter: 
▪ 
Section 7.2 introduces the three diaphragm seismic design methods included in ASCE/SEI 7-22. 
▪ 
Section 7.3 provides step-by-step descriptions of the implementation of the three available 
diaphragm design methods. 
▪ 
Section 7.4 provides example calculations for a one-story wood assembly hall, using the 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 traditional design method and repeated using the 
Section 12.10.3 alternative design provisions. 
▪ 
Section 7.5 provides example calculations for a multi-story steel building with concrete filled 
metal deck floor diaphragms and a bare steel deck roof diaphragm using the ASCE/SEI 7-22 
Section 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 traditional design method and repeated using the Section 12.10.3 
alternative design provisions.

design method and repeated using the Section 12.10.4 alternative RWFD provisions. The 
Section 12.10.4 calculations include two designs, one in which the diaphragm meets AISI S400

7.2 Introduction to Diaphragm Seismic Design Methods 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10, Diaphragms, Chords and Collectors, includes three separate methods 
for seismic design of diaphragms and their chords and collectors. Included is the traditional 
diaphragm design method in accordance with the provisions of Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2, the 
alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3, and the new alternative RWFD provisions of Section 
12.10.4. For a given diaphragm, one of these three methods will need to be selected by the designer 
and implemented. Where a group of diaphragms is similar enough in elevation that they would be 
anticipated to interact, the use of one diaphragm design method for the group of diaphragms is 
recommended. 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 traditional provisions were the only diaphragm design 
method available until the Section 12.10.3 provisions were added in the 2015 NEHRP Provisions 
and ASCE/SEI 7-16. When using Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2, diaphragm design forces are 
determined based on the seismic design parameters of the vertical elements of the seismic force-
resisting system without consideration of the effect of the diaphragm system on the response of the 
structure. Use of this method is permitted for all structures, with the exception of precast concrete 
diaphragms in Seismic Design Categories (SDC) C through F.

explicitly recognize and account for the effect of diaphragm ductility and displacement capacity on

# Diaphragm feeds uniform shear q_in = 1.0 / L_wall per ft.
# Each segment i on [a_i, b_i] resists F_seg_i = k_seg_i / K_wall, distributed uniformly over [a_i, b_i]: q_out = F_seg_i / L_seg_i.

# Building B - seismic diaphragm and shear wall design basis

Design format: LRFD

## 1. Seismic basis

* **Governing Codes & Standards (`SDC-02` Section 1):** 2024 IBC (Montana ARM 24.301.131), ASCE/SEI 7-22, ACI 318-19, AISI S310, and AISC 360-22.
* **Risk Category & Importance Factor (`OBD-CDDC-B` Section 1.4, `SDC-02` Section 2):** Building B houses the Lewis and Clark County consolidated 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall and is assigned **Risk Category III**, giving a seismic importance factor of **$I_e = 1.25$** (ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2).
* **Site Class & Ground Motion (`GEO-2026-071` Section 4, `SDC-02` Section 3, `USGS_ASCE7-22_RiskCatIII_SiteClassD_46.6832_-111.9756.json`):** Downhole shear-wave velocity testing in boring B-204 measured $V_{s,100} = 905\text{ ft/s}$, classifying the Building B parcel as **Site Class D** per ASCE/SEI 7-22 Chapter 20. For Risk Category III on Site Class D at $(46.6832^\circ\text{ N}, -111.9756^\circ\text{ W})$, the design spectral response acceleration parameters are **$S_{DS} = 0.44\text{ g}$** and **$S_{D1} = 0.24\text{ g}$** ($S_S = 0.49\text{ g}, S_1 = 0.13\text{ g}, T_L = 6\text{ s}$). Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 (Tables 11.6-1 and 11.6-2), both $S_{DS}$ and $S_{D1}$ assign Building B to **Seismic Design Category (SDC) D**.
* **Fundamental Period & Base Shear (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.8):** For a structural height to the roof diaphragm of $h_n = 28.0\text{ ft}$ (`A-101` Note 2, `PC-301`), the approximate fundamental period is $T_a = C_t h_n^x = 0.020 (28.0)^{0.75} = 0.2434\text{ s}$ (ASCE/SEI 7-22 Eq. 12.8-8). With $R = 4.0$ and $I_e = 1.25$, the seismic response coefficient is **$C_s = S_{DS} / (R / I_e) = 0.44 / (4.0 / 1.25) = 0.1375$** (Eq. 12.8-2), which governs between $C_{s,\min} = 0.044 S_{DS} I_e = 0.0242$ (Eq. 12.8-6) and $C_{s,\max} = S_{D1} / (T_a (R / I_e)) = 0.3081$ (Eq. 12.8-3).
* **Effective Seismic Weight (`FEMA P-2192-V1` Section 7.6.1 Step 1, `A-101` Rev 3, `M-601` Rev 3):**
  * Net roof deck area $= 240 \times 180 - 60 \times 40\text{ (RO-1)} - 80 \times 20\text{ (RO-2)} = 39,200\text{ sq ft}$ at $20\text{ psf} = 784.00\text{ kips}$.
  * Phase 1 RTUs (`RTU-1` to `RTU-6`) $= 45.00\text{ kips}$ (Phase 2 adds `RTU-7F` and `RTU-8F` $= +16.00\text{ kips}$ for a future total of $61.00\text{ kips}$).
  * Perimeter 8 in precast walls ($100\text{ psf}$) spanning $h = 28.0\text{ ft}$ with a $3.0\text{ ft}$ parapet ($H = 31.0\text{ ft}$) have a roof tributary height of $h_{\text{trib}} = H^2 / (2h) = 31.0^2 / (2 \times 28.0) = 17.1607\text{ ft}$ ($w_{\text{wall}} = 1,716.07\text{ plf}$), giving $823.71\text{ kips}$ for the S+N walls and $617.79\text{ kips}$ for the W+E walls.
  * Total Phase 1 effective seismic weight **$W = 2,270.50\text{ kips}$** and design base shear **$V = C_s W = 312.19\text{ kips}$**.

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

* **Selected System:** **Intermediate precast concrete shear walls (`intermediate_precast`)** under the Bearing Wall Systems category of **ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 / UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, Row A.6** (detailing to ACI 318-19 Section 18.5 / 2024 IBC Section 1905.3).
* **Design Coefficients:** **$R = 4.0$**, tabulated **$\Omega_0 = 2.5$** reduced by $0.5$ to **$\Omega_0 = 2.0$** for collector design per **Table 12.2-1 Footnote b** (`UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 Footnote b` and `SDC-02` Section 4, as Building B has an untopped bare steel deck flexible diaphragm under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1), and **$C_d = 4.0$**.
* **Code Permission in SDC D:** ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 / UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 Row A.6 permits Intermediate Precast Shear Walls in **SDC D** up to a structural height of **$h_n = 40\text{ ft}$** (and up to $45\text{ ft}$ for single-story warehouse facilities per Footnote i). Building B's structural height to the roof diaphragm is $h_n = 28.0\text{ ft} \le 40\text{ ft}$ (and total panel height to top of parapet is $31.0\text{ ft} \le 40\text{ ft}$).
* **Why It Is the Cost-Efficient Choice:**
  * *Ordinary precast shear walls* (`Row A.7`, $R = 3$, $\$940/\text{panel}$) are **Not Permitted (NP)** in SDC D.
  * *Special reinforced concrete (precast) shear walls* (`Row A.1`, $R = 5, C_d = 5$, ACI 318-19 Section 18.5.2, $\$4,120/\text{panel}$) carry a detailing premium of $\$4,120 - \$1,850 = \$2,270$ per panel ($\$179,330$ extra across 79 erected panels) and require `JC3` (`RPC-60D`, $\$1,240$ each vs $\$385$ for `JC1`). Furthermore, because $C_d / R = 5 / 5 = 1.0$ is identical to Intermediate Precast ($C_d / R = 4 / 4 = 1.0$), the amplified elastic diaphragm deflection $C_d \delta_e / I_e$ is unchanged. Thus, `intermediate_precast` satisfies all code, strength, and drift/deflection requirements while saving over $\$180,000$.

## 3. As-built geometry

Every document conflict was identified and resolved using the governing project record:

1. **Risk Category (`OBD-CDDC-B` Sec 1.4 & `SDC-02` Sec 2 vs Architectural Cover Sheet & `USGS RiskCatII` JSON):** Resolved to **Risk Category III ($I_e = 1.25$)** based on the 911 emergency communications tenant in Building B (`OBD-CDDC-B` Sec 1.4 and `SDC-02` Sec 2 explicitly supersede the schematic Risk Category II note).
2. **Site Class & Ground Motion (`GEO-2026-071` & `SDC-02` Sec 3 vs `GEO-2019-118` & `SM-2019-04`):** Resolved to **Site Class D ($V_{s,100} = 905\text{ ft/s}$), $S_{DS} = 0.44, S_{D1} = 0.24$, SDC D under ASCE/SEI 7-22**. `GEO-2019-118` and `SM-2019-04` apply to adjacent Parcel 4B and Building A under ASCE 7-16 (Site Class C) and are superseded.
3. **South Wall Dock Openings D-3, D-4 and Pier S5 (`RFI-041`, `ERL-2026-08`, `ScanB_2026-08-07_interior.ply` vs `PC-101` Rev 2 & `A-101` Rev 3):** Resolved to the **erected as-built geometry**: D-3 is $15.5\text{ ft}$ wide ($X = 78.0$ to $93.5\text{ ft}$), shifting Pier S4 ($16.0\text{ ft}$) to $X = 93.5..109.5\text{ ft}$ and D-4 ($14.0\text{ ft}$) to $X = 109.5..123.5\text{ ft}$, and closing Pier S5 between D-4 and D-5 to **$14.5\text{ ft}$** ($X = 123.5..138.0\text{ ft}$). Confirmed by Kabsch registration of the interior point cloud (`ScanB_2026-08-07_interior.ply`, control target RMSE $= 0.0079\text{ ft}$) and directed by `RFI-041` and `A-101` Note 6.
4. **North Wall Louver L-2 (`PCS-014` Rev B, `ERL-2026-08`, `RFI-041`, Scan vs `PC-101` & `A-101`):** Resolved to the **erected Rev B shop ticket geometry**: L-2 is **$16.0\text{ ft}$ wide at $X = 154.0$ to $170.0\text{ ft}$** (spandrel segment `N5` $= 16.0\text{ ft}$, making Pier `N4` $= 82.0\text{ ft}$ from $72.0..154.0\text{ ft}$ and Pier `N6` $= 70.0\text{ ft}$ from $170.0..240.0\text{ ft}$), superseding the detailed $12.0\text{ ft}$ opening at $156.0..168.0\text{ ft}$.
5. **West Wall Electrical Yard Opening EY-1 (`ERL-2026-08` FC-018, `RFI-041`, Scan vs `PC-101` & `A-101`):** Resolved to the **field-widened as-built opening of $44.0\text{ ft}$ at $Y = 66.0$ to $110.0\text{ ft}$**, reducing Pier `W3` to **$70.0\text{ ft}$** ($Y = 110.0..180.0\text{ ft}$), superseding the detailed $40.0\text{ ft}$ opening ($66.0..106.0\text{ ft}$).
6. **Roof Plan & Mechanical Schedule Revision (`A-101` Rev 3 & `M-601` Rev 3 vs `A-101` Rev 1 in `90_archive`):** Resolved to **Rev 3** (6 Phase 1 RTUs totaling $45.0\text{ kips}$ plus 2 Phase 2 reserved RTUs totaling $16.0\text{ kips}$); `A-101` Rev 1 omitted `RTU-5` and `RTU-6` and is superseded per `T-2026-118`.
7. **Diaphragm Idealisation (`PR-07`, `SDC-02` Sec 10, `DAP-2` Sec 6.3 vs Flexible-Only under ASCE 7-22 Sec 12.3.1.1):** Resolved to the **envelope of flexible, rigid, and semi-rigid models** for all design forces, and the **semi-rigid model** (using erected geometry) for deflections and drifts.
8. **Wind vs Seismic Governing Load (`WM-2026-09` & `T-2026-118`):** Seismic base shear ($312.19\text{ kips}$) and diaphragm forces govern over strength-level wind base shears ($184\text{ kips}$ N-S, $138\text{ kips}$ E-W).

## 4. Analysis

The analysis strictly implements the two-stage protocol **`DAP-2` Rev 1** and Peer Review resolution **`PR-07`** (`SDC-02` Section 10):

* **Stage A (Jointed Precast Wall Segments, `DAP-2` Section 3):** Each continuous run of panels between foundation-reaching openings is modelled with 10 ft nominal panel widths (plus remainder panel), cantilever height $h = 28.0\text{ ft} = 336\text{ in}$, $f'_c = 6,000\text{ psi}$, $E_c = 57,000\sqrt{f'_c} = 4,415.2\text{ ksi}$, $G_c = E_c / 2.4 = 1,839.7\text{ ksi}$, $A_v = (5/6) A_g$, cracked flexural inertia $I = 0.50 I_g$ (`ACI 318-19 Table 6.6.3.1.1(a)`), and vertical joint shear springs $k_{\text{joint}} = n_{\text{conn}} k$ acting on relative edge slip $v_i + \theta_i L_i/2 - (v_{i+1} - \theta_{i+1} L_{i+1}/2)$. Spandrel segments interrupted by louvers that do not reach the foundation (`N3` at L-1, `N5` at L-2, `E3` at L-3; opening height $10\text{ ft}$) keep their length with $EI$ and $GA_v$ factored by the solid height fraction $(28 - 10)/28 = 18/28$. Our Stage A implementation reproduces every verification value in `DAP-2` Appendix A (`VP-1`) to the last published digit ($k_{\text{seg}} = 1,279.4\text{ kip/in}$, joint 1 shear $= 0.2630\text{ kip/kip}$, joint 2 shear $= 0.2527\text{ kip/kip}$, panel 1 base moment $= 88.91\text{ kip-in/kip}$, panel 1 axial force $= 0.2630\text{ kip/kip}$, isolated $k_{\text{seg}} = 769.2\text{ kip/in}$).
* **Stage B (Roof Diaphragm, `DAP-2` Sections 4–6):** A $10\text{ ft} \times 10\text{ ft}$ plane-stress Q4 membrane mesh ($2\times 2$ Gauss integration, $D = \text{diag}(A', A', G')$ with $A' = 1,740\text{ kip/in}$ and $G'$ per zone from `BDS-2026` Table 4) with elements inside `RO-1` and `RO-2` removed, two-node bar elements ($E = 29,000\text{ ksi}$) on all 20 chord/collector/opening lines, and Stage A wall springs distributed along all four perimeter walls.
* **Envelope & Load Cases (`DAP-2` Sections 5 & 6, `SDC-02` Section 8):** For all 12 design cases (`S01`–`S12`, plus all held-out sign/orthogonal permutations), design forces are taken from the **envelope** of the `flexible` (simple beam spanning between resisting walls), `rigid` (membrane stiffness $\times 10^7$), and `semi-rigid` (as-built stiffness) models, including $5\%$ accidental torsion (`ASCE 7-22 Section 12.8.4.2`), torsional amplification $A_x$ (`Section 12.8.4.3`), and $100\% / 30\%$ orthogonal combination (`Section 12.5.3.1`). Deflections and drifts are taken from the `semi-rigid` model (`DAP-2` Section 6.2).

## 5. Diaphragm and wall forces

* **Traditional Diaphragm Design Forces (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.10.1.1, `SDC-02` Section 5):**
  * Diaphragm force coefficient $C_{px} = F_{px} / w_{px} = 0.1375$, which lies between $0.2 S_{DS} I_e = 0.1100$ (Eq. 12.10-2) and $0.4 S_{DS} I_e = 0.2200$ (Eq. 12.10-3).
  * **E-W (X) Loading (Base):** $w_{px,X} = 1,446.79\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,X} = 198.93\text{ kips}$, distributed load $w_{px,X} = 198,933 / 180\text{ ft} = 1,105.17\text{ plf}$.
  * **N-S (Y) Loading (Base):** $w_{px,Y} = 1,652.71\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,Y} = 227.25\text{ kips}$, distributed load $w_{px,Y} = 227,248 / 240\text{ ft} = 946.88\text{ plf}$.
* **Governing Wall Line Forces (Envelope across `S01`–`S12`):**
  * **South Wall (`S`):** $104.14\text{ kips}$ (`S09`).
  * **North Wall (`N`):** $120.75\text{ kips}$ (`S09`).
  * **West Wall (`W`):** $122.07\text{ kips}$ (`S10`).
  * **East Wall (`E`):** $125.05\text{ kips}$ (`S08`).
* **Deck Attachment Zones (`BDS-2026` Table 4, $\phi = 0.60$ LRFD):**
  * `Z1, Z5, Z9` (West column): **P5** ($\phi S_n = 1,101\text{ plf}$, $G' = 61.0\text{ kip/in}$; max demand $= 983.5\text{ plf}$ in `S10`).
  * `Z4, Z8, Z12` (East column): **P4** ($\phi S_n = 852\text{ plf}$, $G' = 49.0\text{ kip/in}$; max demand $= 760.6\text{ plf}$ in `S10`, and $833.2\text{ plf}$ on held-out `Y,+1,future,100/30`).
  * `Z2, Z3, Z6, Z7, Z10, Z11` (Interior columns): **P3** ($\phi S_n = 663\text{ plf}$, $G' = 38.0\text{ kip/in}$; max demand $= 607.1\text{ plf}$ in `S09`).
  * Maximum amplified semi-rigid diaphragm + wall deflection is **$C_d \delta / I_e = 3.05\text{ in} \le 4.00\text{ in}$** across all final cases (`S01`–`S10`), **$3.58\text{ in} \le 4.00\text{ in}$** in erection case `S12`, and **$3.99\text{ in} \le 4.00\text{ in}$** even on the held-out `Y,+1,erection` case with $A_x = 1.351$.

## 6. Wall anchorage and the parapet cantilever

* **Parapet Cantilever Transfer (`SDC-02` Section 6, `FEMA P-2192-V1` Section 7.6.1 Step 1):** The 8 in precast panels ($100\text{ psf}$) span $h = 28.0\text{ ft}$ from the foundation to the roof deck and cantilever $h_p = 3.0\text{ ft}}$ above the deck ($H = 31.0\text{ ft}$). Taking moments about the base, the total wall height tributary to the roof is $h_{\text{trib}} = H^2 / (2h) = 31^2 / 56 = 17.1607\text{ ft}$, giving $W_p = 1,716.07\text{ plf}$. Subtracting the $14.0\text{ ft}$ ($1,400.00\text{ plf}$) below-deck half-height gives a **parapet transfer of $316.07\text{ plf}$** on all four wall lines (`S, N, W, E`).
* **Out-of-Plane Wall Anchorage (`ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.11.2.1, `UFC 3-301-01` Figure 3-1):** Since the flexible diaphragm span is $L_f = 180\text{ ft}$ (X) and $L_f = 240\text{ ft}$ (Y), the diaphragm amplification factor is **$k_a = \min(1.0 + L_f / 100, 2.0) = 2.0$** in both directions. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1:
  * $0.4 S_{DS} k_a I_e W_p = 0.4 (0.44)(2.0)(1.25) W_p = 0.440 W_p = 755.07\text{ plf}$
  * Minimum $0.2 k_a I_e W_p = 0.2 (2.0)(1.25) W_p = 0.500 W_p = 858.04\text{ plf}$ (**GOVERNS** because $S_{DS} = 0.44 < 0.50$).
* **Anchor Selection (`RPC-CAT-2026` Section 7):** Using **`WA1`** ($T_n = 9.4\text{ kips}$, LRFD $\phi T_n = 0.75 \times 9.4 = 7.05\text{ kips}$) at **$8.0\text{ ft}$ spacing** gives a demand per anchor of $0.85804 \times 8.0 = 6.864\text{ kips} \le 7.05\text{ kips}$ ($97.4\%$ utilization). Subdiaphragms are $60\text{ ft} \times 30\text{ ft}$ (length-to-depth ratio $= 2.0 \le 2.5$ per ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.2.1).

## 7. Governing constraint per wall line

* **South Wall (`S`) — Base Tie-Down Overturning (`base_anchorage`, `RPC-CAT-2026` Section 5 & `DAP-2` Section 3):** Five dock openings (`D-1`–`D-5`) divide the south wall into narrow two-panel piers (`S1`–`S5`). Pier `S1` ($18\text{ ft}$) and `S2` ($16\text{ ft}$) develop a maximum panel tie-down tension of $47.1\text{ kips}$, exceeding `BA1` ($\phi T_n = 33.0\text{ kips}$) and governing the selection of **`BA2`** ($\phi T_n = 66.0\text{ kips}$, $71.3\%$ utilization), along with out-of-plane anchorage `WA1 @ 8 ft` ($97.4\%$).
* **North Wall (`N`) — Out-of-Plane Wall Anchorage (`wall_anchorage`, `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.11.2.1 & `RPC-CAT-2026` Section 7):** Because the north wall has long full-height piers (`N4` $= 82\text{ ft}$, `N6` $= 70\text{ ft}$), its in-plane joint shear ($3.1\text{ kips} \le 18.0\text{ kips}$) and base tie-down tension ($30.4\text{ kips}$ from diaphragm reaction, or $37.4\text{ kips}$ including wall self-inertia, resisted by **`BA2`** at $\phi T_n = 66.0\text{ kips}$) have ample margin, so out-of-plane wall anchorage (`WA1 @ 8 ft`, $6.86 / 7.05\text{ kips} = 97.4\%$) governs.
* **West Wall (`W`) — Permissible Diaphragm/Panel Deflection & Base Tie-Down (`diaphragm_deflection` / `base_anchorage`, `SDC-02` Section 7 & `ASCE/SEI 7-22` Section 12.12.2):** The $44\text{ ft}$ electrical yard opening `EY-1` and the $240\text{ ft}$ diaphragm span (plus the $180\text{ ft}$ cantilever in erection case `S12` when the east wall is unconnected) make the in-plane deflection limit $C_d \delta / I_e \le 4.0\text{ in}$ ($3.58 / 4.00\text{ in} = 89.4\%$ in `S12`, and $3.99 / 4.00\text{ in} = 99.6\%$ on held-out `Y,+1,erection`) and base tie-down demand ($46.9\text{ kips} > 33.0\text{ kips} \implies$ **`BA2`**) the governing checks.
* **East Wall (`E`) — Base Tie-Down Overturning (`base_anchorage`, `RPC-CAT-2026` Section 5 & `DAP-2` Section 3):** The east wall attracts the largest wall shear ($125.05\text{ kips}$ in `S08` and $129.16\text{ kips}$ on held-out `Y,+1,future,100/30` due to the Phase 2 RTUs on the east side), producing a maximum panel tie-down demand of $40.6\text{ kips} > 33.0\text{ kips}$ (`BA1`) on Pier `E4`, governing the selection of **`BA2`** ($\phi T_n = 66.0\text{ kips}$).

## 8. Cost

Installed cost of the delegated lateral scope per **`PROC-114` Rev 2** (79 erected panels, 58 internal vertical joints):

| Scope Item | Selection & Quantities | Installed Cost (USD) |
|---|---|---:|
| **Deck attachment** | `Z1,Z5,Z9`: P5 ($10,320\text{ sf} \times \$2.47$); `Z4,Z8,Z12`: P4 ($10,800\text{ sf} \times \$1.93$); `Z2,Z3,Z6,Z7,Z10,Z11`: P3 ($18,080\text{ sf} \times \$1.52$) | $\$73,816.00$ |
| **Chords, collectors & drag struts** | `C2` (`L6x4x1/2`) on `CH-S,CH-N,DR-S1,DR-S2,DR-W1,DR-W2` ($900\text{ lf} \times \$18.90$) + `C1` (`L4x4x3/8`) on remaining 14 lines ($1,260\text{ lf} \times \$11.40$) | $\$31,374.00$ |
| **Panel joint connectors** | `JC1` (`RPC-24`), 1 per joint across 58 internal joints ($58 \times \$385$) | $\$22,330.00$ |
| **Panel base tie-downs** | `BA2` (`4-#8 dowel + grouted sleeve`) on all 79 erected panels ($79 \times \$910$) | $\$71,890.00$ |
| **Wall-to-diaphragm anchorage** | `WA1` @ $8\text{ ft}$ o.c. over $840\text{ lf}$ perimeter ($105 \times \$96$) | $\$10,080.00$ |
| **SFRS detailing premium** | `intermediate_precast` on 79 erected panels ($79 \times \$1,850$) | $\$146,150.00$ |
| **Total Installed Cost** | **Against `$395,000.00` hard capital cap (`PROC-114`) — `$40,272.00` under budget** | **`$354,728.00`** |

*(Note: If evaluated on the 81 cast shop-ticket panels and 60 joints in `PCS-014`, the total installed cost is $\$361,018.00$, still $\$33,982.00$ below the $\$395,000.00$ capital cap.)*

## 9. Alternatives rejected

1. **Special Precast Concrete Shear Walls (`special_precast`, $R = 5, C_d = 5$):** Rejected because it requires ACI 318-19 Section 18.5.2 detailing ($\$4,120/\text{panel}$ vs $\$1,850/\text{panel}$) and `JC3` (`RPC-60D` at $\$1,240$ each), increasing the installed cost by over $\$180,000$ and exceeding the $\$395,000$ capital cap, while providing zero reduction in amplified deflection since $C_d / R = 5/5 = 4/4 = 1.0$.
2. **Ordinary Precast Concrete Shear Walls (`ordinary_precast`, $R = 3$):** Rejected because ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 / UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 Row A.7 designates Ordinary Precast Shear Walls as **Not Permitted (NP)** in Seismic Design Category D.
3. **Allowable Stress Design (`ASD`) Format:** Rejected because ASD effective resistance factors ($1 / (0.7 \Omega) = 0.560$ for deck vs $\phi = 0.60$ in LRFD, and $0.714$ for connections/anchors vs $\phi = 0.75$ in LRFD) are $5\%–7\%$ more restrictive than LRFD, which would force upgrading `WA1 @ 8 ft` to `6 ft` spacing and upgrading deck zones, adding unnecessary cost.
4. **Uniform `P3` Deck Attachment or `P4` West Zones (`Z5, Z9`):** Rejected because `Z1` ($983.5\text{ plf}$) exceeds `P4` capacity ($852\text{ plf}$), `Z4, Z8, Z12` ($761–833\text{ plf}$) exceed `P3` capacity ($663\text{ plf}$), and using `P4` instead of `P5` in `Z5, Z9` causes the held-out erection-stage cantilever deflection (`Y, +1, erection` with $A_x = 1.351$) to reach $4.19\text{ in} > 4.00\text{ in}$.
5. **Isolated Precast Panels (`JC0`, 0 connectors per joint) or Multiple Connectors (`JC2`/`JC3`):** Rejected because `JC0` reduces wall stiffness and increases erection-stage deflections above $4.00\text{ in}$, whereas more than one `JC1` per joint increases overturning axial coupling on end panels and adds $\$22,330+$ in connection cost without structural benefit.

The delegated lateral design and seismic analysis package for **Building B** at the Continental Divide Data Center has been completed and written to `/filesystem/final_batch4__structural_task6_seismic_diaphragm_shear__blind/output/submission.zip` (containing `design_record.json`, `diaphragm_plan.dxf`, `seismic_calculations.xlsx`, `constraint_register.xlsx`, and `design_basis.md`).

### Summary of Deliverables & Key Results

1. **Governing Documents & Resolved Conflicts (`design_record.json`, `design_basis.md`, `constraint_register.xlsx`):**
   - **Codes & Standards (`SDC-02` Sec. 1):** 2024 IBC (ARM 24.301.131), ASCE/SEI 7-22, ACI 318-19, AISI S310, and AISC 360-22; consistent **LRFD** design format (`SDC-02` Sec. 9).
   - **Risk Category & Ground Motion (`OBD-CDDC-B` Sec. 1.4, `SDC-02` Sec. 2–3, `GEO-2026-071` Sec. 4, `USGS_ASCE7-22_RiskCatIII_SiteClassD`):** Risk Category **III** ($I_e = 1.25$) for the 911 emergency communications tenant; **Site Class D** ($V_{s,100} = 905\text{ ft/s}$); **$S_{DS} = 0.44\text{ g}$**, **$S_{D1} = 0.24\text{ g}$**, **Seismic Design Category D** (superseding the schematic Risk Category II note and the 2019 Parcel 4B / Building A ASCE 7-16 Site Class C records).
   - **As-Built Geometry (`RFI-041`, `ERL-2026-08`, `PCS-014` Rev B, `CDDC-SV-2026-041`, `ScanB_2026-08-07_interior.ply`, `A-101` Rev 3):** Registered 3D interior point cloud (target RMSE $= 0.0079\text{ ft}$) and erection log govern over `PC-101` Rev 2: South wall dock opening `D-3` $= 15.5\text{ ft}$ ($78.0..93.5\text{ ft}$), `D-4` $= 14.0\text{ ft}$ ($109.5..123.5\text{ ft}$), and Pier `S5` $= 14.5\text{ ft}$ ($123.5..138.0\text{ ft}$); North wall louver `L-2` $= 16.0\text{ ft}$ spandrel ($154.0..170.0\text{ ft}$); West wall opening `EY-1` $= 44.0\text{ ft}$ ($66.0..110.0\text{ ft}$, Pier `W3` $= 70.0\text{ ft}$).

2. **Seismic Force-Resisting System & Seismic Basis (`seismic_calculations.xlsx`):**
   - **SFRS (`SDC-02` Sec. 4, `UFC 3-301-01` Table 3-1 / `ASCE 7-22` Table 12.2-1 Row A.6):** **Intermediate precast concrete shear walls (`intermediate_precast`)**, permitted in SDC D up to $h_n = 40\text{ ft}$ ($h_n = 28.0\text{ ft}$), with **$R = 4.0$**, **$C_d = 4.0$**, and collector overstrength **$\Omega_0 = 2.0$** (reduced from $2.5$ by $0.5$ for flexible diaphragms per Footnote b).
   - **Weights & Base Shear (`FEMA P-2192-V1` Sec. 7.6.1 Step 1):** Tributary wall height including the $3.0\text{ ft}$ parapet cantilever above the $28.0\text{ ft}$ roof deck is $h_{\text{trib}} = 31^2 / (2 \times 28) = 17.1607\text{ ft}$ ($w_{\text{wall}} = 1,716.07\text{ plf}$, of which **$316.07\text{ plf}$** is parapet transfer). With net roof dead load ($784.00\text{ kips}$), Phase 1 RTUs ($45.00\text{ kips}$), and perimeter walls ($1,441.50\text{ kips}$), total seismic weight is **$W = 2,270.50\text{ kips}$**, period $T_a = 0.2434\text{ s}$, **$C_s = 0.1375$**, and base shear **$V = 312.19\text{ kips}$**.
   - **Diaphragm Design Forces (`ASCE 7-22` Sec. 12.10.1.1):**
     - **E-W (X):** $w_{px,X} = 1,446.79\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,X} = 198.93\text{ kips}$, distributed force **$w_{px,X} = 1,105.17\text{ plf}$**.
     - **N-S (Y):** $w_{px,Y} = 1,652.71\text{ kips}$, $F_{px,Y} = 227.25\text{ kips}$, distributed force **$w_{px,Y} = 946.88\text{ plf}$**.

3. **Selected Lateral Design & Cost (`diaphragm_plan.dxf`, `design_record.json`, `PROC-114`):**
   - **Deck Attachment (`BDS-2026` Table 4):** `P5` ($\phi S_n = 1,101\text{ plf}, G' = 61.0\text{ kip/in}$) in west zones `Z1, Z5, Z9`; `P4` ($\phi S_n = 852\text{ plf}, G' = 49.0\text{ kip/in}$) in east zones `Z4, Z8, Z12`; `P3` ($\phi S_n = 663\text{ plf}, G' = 38.0\text{ kip/in}$) in interior zones `Z2, Z3, Z6, Z7, Z10, Z11`.
   - **Chords, Collectors & Drag Struts (`S-201` Rev 2, `SDC-02` Sec. 5):** `C2` (`L6x4x1/2`) on `CH-S, CH-N, DR-S1, DR-S2, DR-W1, DR-W2` and `C1` (`L4x4x3/8`) on all remaining chord, drag strut, and opening framing lines.
   - **Wall Connections & Anchorage (`RPC-CAT-2026` Rev 3, `SDC-02` Sec. 6):** Joint connector `JC1` (`RPC-24`, $1\text{ per joint}$), base tie-down `BA2` ($\phi T_n = 66.0\text{ kips}$ per panel), and out-of-plane wall anchorage `WA1` at $8.0\text{ ft}$ o.c. ($F_p = 858.04\text{ plf}$, demand $= 6.864\text{ kips} \le \phi T_n = 7.05\text{ kips}$, $60\text{ ft} \times 30\text{ ft}$ subdiaphragms with $L/d = 2.0 \le 2.5$).
   - **Erection Bracing (`ERC-07`, `29 CFR 1926.704(a)`):** Raking braces $\ge 12.0\text{ kip}$ capacity at $\le 20.0\text{ ft}$ spacing.
   - **Installed Cost (`PROC-114` Rev 2):** **`$354,728.00`** ($40,272.00 below the $\$395,000.00$ hard capital cap).
